correctness.rationale: Verified entire analytic proof for real 0<t<=1: dual Lip0 ball K_t is defined by six coordinate and six difference half-spaces. Any Euclidean quadratic comparison is averaged over S3 without worsening two-sided inequalities, yielding q_r=sum(x_i-xbar)^2+3r*xbar^2 for r>0. All 14 vertices give M(r)=max{3r,2t²/3+(3-t)²r/3}. Difference facets give exact minimum t²/2 at (t/2,-t/2,0); coordinate facets via x=(1,s,s) yield min{3r/(1+2r),t²/2} globally. The quotient strictly decreases to r0=t²/[2(3-t²)] and increases afterward, proving unique global optimum and d_BM²=(7-2t-t²)/(3-t²). Derivative -2(t-3)(t-1)/(3-t²)²<0 for 0<t<1, endpoint t=1 gives 2; t->0 limit 7/3 is not the dimension-collapsed t=0 metric. Independent exact-rational 12-halfspace vertex enumeration and sampled invariant-form comparisons for seven rationals including t=1, plus symbolic derivative, corroborate (not prove) the universal result. Arbitrary real linear maps covered by quadratic-form symmetry averaging. All seven actual package files inspected and Git tree matched.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge qualified PASS for the explicit exact Hilbert distortion of the 3+1 four-point ultrametric for all 0<t<=1. The earlier equiradial star theorem uses hub radius <= leaf distance, but after normalization this family lies on the opposite side (hub radius 1/t>1), so direct theorem implication fails for t<1; its closely related finite-candidate machinery is a serious potential extrapolation risk. Another contemporaneous published theorem has the identical scalar function for a different one-short-edge metric, not an isometric/corollary identification of the 3+1 ultrametric. Equilateral endpoint t=1 is known. General finite ultrametric l1-bounds, graph isometries and cone/sum comparisons do not yield the stated all-t Euclidean optimum. Complete primary/published material was compared, but chronology and possible equivalent optimal-ellipsoid treatments remain unresolved bibliographic risks; these do not themselves prove coverage or novelty.
residual_risks: The very close equiradial-star all-m proof algebraically extends to alpha=2/t-1>1 in several steps; a historical all-positive-alpha version could dominate the current exact profile. Its *published theorem statement* is limited to alpha in [0,1].

The one-short-edge deformation record states exactly the same rational expression for a nonisometric object; possible deeper transformation of Banach-Mazur constants beyond isometry is not wholly excluded.
Contemporaneous October 11 2026 publication dates do not establish precise priority ordering or logical derivation chronology.
Older unindexed convex-body optimized-ellipsoid formula or dissertation might coincide. Searches do not prove universal novelty.

value.rationale: The exact Banach-Mazur distance to a Euclidean three-space is a natural intrinsic quantitative invariant of finite Lipschitz-free spaces. The 3+1 clustered four-point ultrametric is one of the natural combinatorial types of four-point ultrametrics; the theorem provides the entire continuous aspect-ratio classification and an optimal ellipsoid, strict interpolation from the l1-type collapsed limit to the equilateral endpoint, not a handpicked isolated constant. Neither known equilateral endpoint nor near-neighbor one-edge metric directly determines this nonisometric family's exact sharp invariant, although the related published star techniques moderate independent methodological significance.
